newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH OPTIMISTIC AFTER HAMMERING SCOTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH OPTIMISTIC AFTER HAMMERING SCOTS.

text.p: England already have their sights set on Ireland in a fortnight's time after burying Scotland with a late barrage of points in their opening Five Nations match on Saturday.
Coach Jack Rowell felt the record 41-13 victory over the luckless Scots answered critics of his regime and claimed his side's strong second-half performance was proof his team were beginning to gel.
"They came out in the second-half with some psychological voltage and cut loose," said Rowell, accused this week by former team manager Geoff Cooke of talking tactical "mumbo-jumbo".

His captain Phil de Glanville, who scored his second try for his country in the high-scoring final phase of the game, acknowledged there had been deficiencies but was delighted that England had ended their four-year try drought against the Scots.
"In the end it was a good all-round performance," he said. "As the opportunities and space came in the second-half we made the most of them."
England must now travel to Dublin to face the Irish, narrow victors over the Welsh, while the Scots attempt to pick up the pieces of a disastrous start to the season.
They have conceded 75 points in two matches and captain Rob Wainwright did not mince words. "We've got to look at ourselves. Our defence just wasn't good enough," he said.
Team manager Arthur Hastie said the Scots were "a bit mystified" by some of the refereeing decisions but conceded: "We were probably beaten by a much better side."
